0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard was' tion on 1 August 1965, after Chemical Analysis Sectional Structural and Metals Division
adopted by the Indian Standards Instituthe draft finalized by the Methods of Committee had been approved by the . Council.

0.2 Cadmium copper is used for making wire for telegraphic and telephone Suitable methods have been laid down in this standard to purposes. determine its chemical composition. 0.3 In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in the country. This has been met by deriving assistance from the `Book of ASTM Methods of chemical analysis of metals', 1962, published by the American Society for Testing and Materials. 0.4 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

4.2.1 Cathode - It may be formed or from wire gauze.

from plain or perforated

4.2.1.1 Gauze ca.thodes made preferably from gauze containing 400 mesh/ems should be used. The wire used for making gauze should be approximately 0.20 mm in diameter. Cathodes should be stiffened by doubling the gauze for about 3 mm on the top and bottom or by reinforcing the gauze at the top and bottom with a platinum ring or \ band. 3

IS : 3186 - 1965 4.2.1.2 The diameter and height of the cylinder should be approxiThe stem should be made from mately 30 mm and 50 mm respectively. platinum alloy wire such as platinum-iridium, platinum-rhodium or platinum-ruthenium having diameter of approximately 1.5 mm. It should The overall be flattened and welded to the entire height of the gauze. height of the cathode including the stem should approximately be 130 mm.
The 4.2.2 Anode - Either a spiral or a gauze anode should be used. spiral anode should be made from 1.0 mm or larger platinum wire formed into a spiral of seven coils with a height of approximately 50 mm and diameter of 12 mm, the overall height including the stem being 130 mm. The gauze anode should be made of the same material and of the same general design as platinum gauze cathode specified under 4.2.1. 4.3

Reagent

4.3.1 Sulphuric Acid-Nitric Acid MixtureAdd slowly, with constant stirring, 300 mI of concenfrated sulphuric acid (sp gr I-84; conforming to IS : 266-1961* ) to 750 ml of water, cool, add 210 ml of concentrated nitric acid ( sp gr 1.42; conforming to IS : 264-1950t ).
4.3.2 4.4 Ethano! or Methanol 95 percent ( v/v) .

Procedure

4.4.1 Transfer 2 g of an accurately weighed sample into a 250-ml beaker provided with a cover glass and add 20 ml of sulphuric acid-nitric acid mixture. After the initial reaction is over, heat to 80" to 90�C until completely dissolved and brown fumes and expelled.
4.4.2 Wash down the cover and sides of the beaker and dilute the solution to 200 ml. Add 2 g of urea, insert the electrodes, the cathode having been accurately weighed; cover with a pair of split cover glass and electrolyze for 16 hours at a current density of 0.6 A/dm2 (at this current density, the electrolysis is conveniently carried on overnight ), or at a In the current density of 4 A/dm2 for a short period (about 2.5 hours). latter case, one of the types of rotating forms of electrodes generally available may be used. When the solution becomes colourless reduce the current density to 0.3 A/dm2 and continue electrolysis until the deposition of copper is complete as indicated ,by absence of plating on the new surface of the electrode obtained by raising the level of the solution.

4.4.3 Without interrupting the current, raise the electrode assembly. While raising, rinse .thoroughly with water and collect the washings into the electrolyte. Remove the cathode quickly while washing further with
*Specification for sulphuric acid ( m&d).
j-Specification for nitric acid.

IS : 3186 - 1965 water; rinse it with water in a beaker and then dip it in two successive Dry the cathode in an air oven at 110�C baths of ethanol or methanol. for three to five minutes, cool and weigh for copper. Preserve the electrolyte for the determination .of cadmium. 4.5 Calculation Copper, percent =$x where

5.1 Outline of the MethodCadmium is precipitated,from the electrolyte preserved under 4.4.3 by diethyldithiocarbamate; dissolved in hydrochloric acid and determined volumetrically by titration with EDTA. 5.2 Reagents 5.2.1 Tartaric Acid Solution (300 g/l) -Dissolve 300 g of tartaric acid in 700 ml of water with heat, cool to room temperature, and dilute to one lilxe. 5.2.2 Methyl. Red Indicator Solution ( 0.4 g/l) -Dissolve 0.1 g of methyl red in 3.72 ml of 0.100 0 N Sodium hydroxide solution and dilute to 250 ml with water. Filter if necessary. 5.2.3 Sodium Hydroxide Solution ( 200 g/l ) -Dissolve 200 g of sodium hydroxide in 800 ml of water, cool to room temperature, and dilute to one litre.
5.2.4 Potassium Cyanide ( 100 g/Z)--Dissolve in 500 ml of water and dilute to one litre.
